questions.question: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act phase. When can they first win as Usurper, and what happens if someone takes the title away meanwhile?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: At their next Wake they check victory before flipping Oathkeeper to Usurper, so cannot yet win as Usurper; if still Usurper at the following Wake they win. Losing the title prevents this; a new holder receives it Oathkeeper-side. At end of round eight an existing Usurper can win under the ordered endgame rules.
questions.observed_answer: The Exile cannot win as Usurper in the same Act. At their next Wake, they first check for victory while still Oathkeeper; then, if still holding title, flip it to Usurper. Their first Usurper win check is the following Wake, unless round 8 ends first while they remain Usurper. Losing the title prevents the win; retaking it resets the title to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.

questions.question: List all four Oaths, their matching Visions, and the extra universal requirement for a Visionary win. Do ties for most count for a Vision?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Supremacy/Conquest: most sites; People/Rebellion: People’s Favor; Protection/Sanctuary: most relics and banners combined; Devotion/Faith: Darkest Secret. Exile must have the Vision revealed, fulfill it at Wake (or the round-eight check), and at least three Visions must have been drawn from the world deck. Most means strictly more than every other player, not a tie.
questions.observed_answer: The Oaths and matching true Visions are Supremacy—Conquest (rule the most sites); People—Rebellion (hold People’s Favor); Protection—Sanctuary (hold the most relics and banners); Devotion—Faith (hold Darkest Secret). A Visionary win also requires the Exile to have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 world-deck Visions drawn by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, “most” means strictly more than every other player; a tie does not count.

questions.question: What happens in Rest, in order, and how do Citizen Supply and saved Supply work?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Return favor from denizens/edifices to matching banks; secrets from denizens/edifices/relics to acting board and flip own facedown secrets up; Exile/Chancellor refresh to personal-bank-warband space, Citizen to exact Chancellor marker space including leftmost; add remaining unspent Supply by moving left, capped at leftmost; optional Rest powers once each any order.
questions.observed_answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown board secrets faceup; (3) Exile/Chancellor refresh Supply to the space for warbands remaining in their personal bank (Chancellor: 18+→6, 11–17→5, 4–10→4, 0–3→3; Exile: 9+→6, 4–8→5, 0–3→4); Citizen refreshes to the Chancellor’s exact marker space. Then (4) save remaining unspent Supply by moving marker one extra space left per point, capped at leftmost/7 Supply; (5) optional Rest powers.

questions.question: How do adviser limits, facedown restrictions, revealing later, and replacing a true Vision work?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Three advisers including facedown; facedown has no suit/banner/power, any card can be held thus. Before playing over limit discard an adviser, respecting locks and any new changed limit. Minor action may play facedown adviser faceup as searched (site/advisers/revealed Vision as legal) or discard it. True faceup Vision only Exile revealed slot, not adviser, replaces/discards existing Vision. Cannot simply discard faceup adviser at will.
questions.observed_answer: There may be up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser if permitted; locks still apply. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction, or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup legally or discarded as a minor action; a faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will. A revealed true Vision goes in the Exile’s separate Revealed Vision space, not an adviser slot, and replaces/discards the previous revealed true Vision.

questions.question: How do you Recover a relic versus either banner, and what happens to the old banner resources?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: 1 Supply; facedown relic at pawn site only at printed site cost, then take faceup personal bank. Either banner from anywhere, even yourself: pay more favor/secrets than old amount, stack new payment. People’s Favor flips off Mob and old favor distributes singly along banks away from deck from any starting suit wrapping. Darkest Secret: take one old secret, previous holder gets rest (self gets all; bank remainder stays bank).
questions.observed_answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus target cost. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost and hold it faceup in your personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere (including you or shared bank). For People’s Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently has, add payment to it, distribute its old favor one at a time through suit banks starting at a chosen bank, then flip Mob to normal; no seizure penalty applies. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it has, place them on it, take 1 old secret and give the rest to prior holder (if yourself, all old secrets return to you; shared-bank remainder stays there).

questions.question: When is another player’s Darkest Secret safe or recoverable? Include no advisers, no cards, and a ruin-only site.
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Recoverable if at least one suited card at holder’s pawn site matches none of their faceup advisers; no faceup advisers does not protect it if suited card exists. Empty/ruin-only site protects it; ignore suits absent on ruins/facedown advisers. Can recover from self or shared bank freely, still paying cost.
questions.observed_answer: Another player’s Darkest Secret is recoverable only if their pawn’s site has at least one suited card whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers; one mismatch suffices even if other cards match. Thus a site with no suited cards is safe, and a ruin-only site is safe (ruins have no suit). With no faceup advisers, any suited card at the site is unmatched and permits recovery. Self-recovery and recovery from shared bank ignore this protection.

questions.question: Explain legal Campaign defender and target selection, including remote sites and a same-site relic target.
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: 2 Supply; defender another player ruling pawn site or whose pawn there, or bandits if no player rules it. At least one target at pawn site; if defender rules it must target it. May target any defender sites anywhere; relics/banners or pawn+favor only if their pawn is at attacker site. Relic target of co-located defender satisfies local target requirement. Pawn+favor adds two defense dice; sites one each; relic printed shields; banners resource count.
questions.observed_answer: Choose any other player who rules your site or has their pawn there as defender. If no player rules your site, bandits may be chosen. At least one target must be at your pawn’s site; if defender rules that site, you must target it. You may add any defender sites elsewhere on the map, one defense die each. If defender’s pawn is at your site, you may also target their relics, banners, or pawn and favor together; those co-located targets use their printed dice and a same-site relic itself satisfies the local-target requirement.

fact_checks.expected_fact: Defender is another player ruling attacker site or with pawn there; bandits may be chosen if no player rules site.
fact_checks.reason: The cited same-entry passage states the required rule, including its applicable conditions.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Vow an Oath:** won by Vision alone → next Oath matches that Vision. Any other way or multiple victory methods → choose any Oath **except current one**. Save goal in World Box.
2. **Free Chronicle Citizenship (ignore normal offers):** no Reliquary relic, resource payment or Scepter permission is required. If winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must do both: **flip their board to Citizen** and **replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site**, regardless of the old garrison size. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.
3. **Map and edifices:** Imperial winner may build **or** repair **one** edifice. At ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace denizen with matching intact Archive edifice, returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return relics to relic deck and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner does not rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside **all sites with ruins**, with attached ruins, remaining denizens and relics, in map order top Cradle to bottom Hinterland. Remove pawns/favor/secrets/warbands from map.
4. **Repack map slots:** excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland in top-down order. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots **bottom-up** with set-aside ruins **bottom-up**, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill any remaining slots with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top one up.
5. **Add 6 denizens:** winner's most common adviser suit determines 3 random Archive cards, next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise suit 1, to world deck. Choose among tied suits; no suited advisers → choose any. Suit cycle Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord. If Archive cannot supply the full allocation, do **not** add that allocation: heal Archive instead. Sort all Dispossessed by suit; take 6 random from largest Dispossessed suit stack into world deck; shuffle remaining Dispossessed into matching Archive suit stacks.
6. **Dispossess 6:** set aside all 5 Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles with **losers' advisers**, move 6 random cards unseen to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded from this pool.
7. **Relics:** save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to printed number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.
8. **Save world:** stack each site's attached cards on it, stack sites so top Cradle on top and bottom Hinterland at bottom, put in World Box. Save player boards on current Exile/Citizen sides. Next game may have different people: after seats are assigned, non-Chancellors choose among these boards on their saved sides in turn order, rather than automatically inheriting a particular person’s former board.
9. **Rebuild world deck:** shuffle all denizens remaining in play (not those retained at sites/Archive/Dispossessed). Top stack **10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12**; middle **15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18**; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. Chronicle aid's printed “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; do not make a 14-card top stack.

questions.question: In later-game setup with five players, how much favor goes in each bank, what is on the banners, and what resources and warbands start on each kind of player board?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Four favor per suit bank (three with two–four players). People’s Favor normal with one favor, Darkest Secret one secret. Chancellor two favor,one secret,three purple board warbands; other players one favor,one secret,three board warbands (own color Exile,purple Citizen). All full Supply.
questions.observed_answer: With 5 players, put 4 favor in each suit bank. People’s Favor starts normal with 1 favor; Darkest Secret starts with 1 secret. Chancellor starts with 2 favor, 1 secret, and 3 purple warbands on board. Each Exile or Citizen starts with 1 favor and 1 secret; Exiles have 3 own-color warbands on board, Citizens 3 purple. All have full leftmost Supply.

evidence.excerpt:
1. Deal saved sites with attached denizens, edifices and relics to map slots: Cradle fully, then Provinces, then Hinterland, top to bottom. Start round 1 and Visions Drawn 0; use saved goal reference.
2. Collect shared pieces and both banners. People's Favor begins normal side with 1 favor; Darkest Secret has 1 secret. Put **3 favor per suit bank**, or **4 each with 5–6 players**.
3. Choose Chancellor by any method (previous winner recommended, not required), seated at Cradle, others randomly. Chancellor takes purple pieces, board, Reliquary and Grand Scepter. Other players in turn order choose a board on its saved Exile or Citizen side and corresponding color's pieces. Starting Citizens receive no Reliquary relic.
4. All start at full leftmost Supply. Chancellor has 2 favor, 1 secret and 3 purple warbands on board; place 2 purple warbands on topmost faceup Cradle site and 1 at each other faceup site with a denizen or intact edifice. Chancellor begins as Oathkeeper; additionally takes Darkest Secret for Devotion or People's Favor for People.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

questions.question: Which winner can build or repair an edifice in Chronicle, how many, where, and may a new edifice replace a denizen at a site already holding a ruin?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Only Chancellor/Citizen winner,one build or repair. Build at ruled site with no edifice intact or ruined,replace matching denizen by intact Archive edifice,denizen to world deck. Or repair ruled ruin by flipping intact. No building over an existing ruin.
questions.observed_answer: Only an Imperial Chronicle winner may build or repair one edifice. At a ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace a denizen with matching intact Archive edifice and return denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. A site already holding a ruin is not eligible for building a new edifice, since it does not meet “no intact or ruined edifice.”

fact_checks.expected_fact: Chancellor/Citizen winner may build or repair one.
fact_checks.reason: The cited same-entry passage states the required rule, including its applicable conditions.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Vow an Oath:** won by Vision alone → next Oath matches that Vision. Any other way or multiple victory methods → choose any Oath **except current one**. Save goal in World Box.
2. **Free Chronicle Citizenship (ignore normal offers):** no Reliquary relic, resource payment or Scepter permission is required. If winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must do both: **flip their board to Citizen** and **replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site**, regardless of the old garrison size. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.
3. **Map and edifices:** Imperial winner may build **or** repair **one** edifice. At ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace denizen with matching intact Archive edifice, returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return relics to relic deck and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner does not rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside **all sites with ruins**, with attached ruins, remaining denizens and relics, in map order top Cradle to bottom Hinterland. Remove pawns/favor/secrets/warbands from map.
4. **Repack map slots:** excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland in top-down order. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots **bottom-up** with set-aside ruins **bottom-up**, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill any remaining slots with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top one up.
5. **Add 6 denizens:** winner's most common adviser suit determines 3 random Archive cards, next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise suit 1, to world deck. Choose among tied suits; no suited advisers → choose any. Suit cycle Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord. If Archive cannot supply the full allocation, do **not** add that allocation: heal Archive instead. Sort all Dispossessed by suit; take 6 random from largest Dispossessed suit stack into world deck; shuffle remaining Dispossessed into matching Archive suit stacks.
6. **Dispossess 6:** set aside all 5 Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles with **losers' advisers**, move 6 random cards unseen to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded from this pool.
7. **Relics:** save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to printed number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.
8. **Save world:** stack each site's attached cards on it, stack sites so top Cradle on top and bottom Hinterland at bottom, put in World Box. Save player boards on current Exile/Citizen sides. Next game may have different people: after seats are assigned, non-Chancellors choose among these boards on their saved sides in turn order, rather than automatically inheriting a particular person’s former board.
9. **Rebuild world deck:** shuffle all denizens remaining in play (not those retained at sites/Archive/Dispossessed). Top stack **10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12**; middle **15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18**; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. Chronicle aid's printed “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; do not make a 14-card top stack.

A site already holding a ruin is not eligible for building a new edifice, since it does not meet “no intact or ruined edifice.”

questions.question: A matching-suit card is played to a Homeland site after a different-suit card was discarded there this turn. Does reward trigger, what can reward be, and how is a relic reward resolved?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Yes provided no card of matching Homeland suit was discarded there this turn. Printed reward: favor or secret from matching bank/shared bank,or two warbands,or take site relic treating as Recover (no ordinary Recover action/site cost). Gain site-play favor then Homeland effect before When Played.
questions.observed_answer: Yes. Printed reward may be a shared-bank secret, favor from matching bank, 2 warbands, or its relic treated as Recover. Resolve normal site-play favor, then Homeland reward, then When Played effect. Taking a relic this way costs no Supply or ordinary site resource cost.

evidence.excerpt:
- **Opportunity** (Salt Flats/Mine/Drowned City): at end of your Wake take 1 favor/secret from site, optionally.
- **Homeland** sites: when you play a matching-suit card there and have not discarded a card **of that same suit at that site this turn**, gain its printed reward: 1 secret from shared bank, favor from matching suit bank, 2 warbands, or take its relic treating this as Recover. Discarding a different suit there does not suppress it. Taking the relic by this power costs neither Supply nor the ordinary site resource cost. Resolve normal site-play favor first, then the Homeland reward, then the played card’s When Played power.
- **Coasts:** traveling from one Coast to another costs 1 Supply and ignores Narrow Pass.
- **Plains/Mountain:** must add/subtract 1 attack die when site or anything at site is targeted, even if attacker rules it.
- **River:** Muster there gains 1 additional warband if you rule it.
- **Charming Valley:** traveling from it increases Travel cost by 1.
- **Shrouded Wood:** travel from it has a fixed base cost of 2 before other modifiers, ignoring Narrow Pass and Hidden Place; if enemy rules it, travel to site of ruler's choice (Chancellor chooses for Empire), even when someone else makes you travel. Banishment spends no Supply but still obeys this destination choice.
- **Narrow Pass:** entering its region from another must travel to it; targeting anything in its region from another region must also target it unless you rule it.
- **Great Slum:** when playing/moving a card there, may first discard a card there.
- **Marshes:** Search while pawn there draws 1 fewer card.
- **Buried Giant:** traveling from it may flip 1 own board secret facedown to spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass.
- **Hidden Place:** cannot travel there or declare Campaign targets there unless flipping 1 board secret facedown.
- **Tribunal:** Action if you rule it or pawn there: negotiate binding immediate exchanges of favor and secrets, as well as binding future actions in combination with any player and agreed penalties. This does not grant unrestricted immediate relic/banner transfers.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. 1. **Vow an Oath:** won by Vision alone → next Oath matches that Vision. Any other way or multiple victory methods → choose any Oath **except current one**. Save goal in World Box.
2. **Free Chronicle Citizenship (ignore normal offers):** no Reliquary relic, resource payment or Scepter permission is required. If winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must do both: **flip their board to Citizen** and **replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site**, regardless of the old garrison size. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.
3. **Map and edifices:** Imperial winner may build **or** repair **one** edifice. At ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace denizen with matching intact Archive edifice, returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return relics to relic deck and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner does not rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside **all sites with ruins**, with attached ruins, remaining denizens and relics, in map order top Cradle to bottom Hinterland. Remove pawns/favor/secrets/warbands from map.
4. **Repack map slots:** excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland in top-down order. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots **bottom-up** with set-aside ruins **bottom-up**, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill any remaining slots with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top one up.
5. **Add 6 denizens:** winner's most common adviser suit determines 3 random Archive cards, next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise suit 1, to world deck. Choose among tied suits; no suited advisers → choose any. Suit cycle Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord. If Archive cannot supply the full allocation, do **not** add that allocation: heal Archive instead. 6. **Dispossess 6:** set aside all 5 Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles with **losers' advisers**, move 6 random cards unseen to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded from this pool.
7. **Relics:** save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to printed number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.

Top stack **10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12**; middle **15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18**; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. questions.question: If a victorious attacker targeted pawn/favor and a banner, must they banish, must they burn favor, and must they take the banner? What is the rounding of board favor burn?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Banish optional;board favor burn independently optional,half rounded down. Taking all targeted relics/banners mandatory. Seized banner burns two its resources min one separately from optional board-favor burn.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

On attacker victory after targeting pawn/favor and a banner, banishment is optional, board-favor burn is independently optional, and taking all targeted banners is mandatory. If choosing favor burn, burn half the defender’s board favor rounded down.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. questions.question: Unless an effect specifies different locations, where do favor/secrets, an adviser card, and a relic move when you Take them? How does Give reverse the direction? Recovering from self or shared bank ignores this protection.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

questions.question: Describe the Chronicle’s new Oath choice, Citizenship turnover, and world-deck rebuilding, including why the top stack is not 14 cards.
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Vision-only winner uses matching Oath; other/multiple-method win chooses any different Oath. Exile winner flips all Citizens even boxed to Exile then may offer other Exiles except newly flipped; accepted map garrisons replaced one each by winner warband (ignore normal offer). Rebuild remaining denizens: ten+two random Visions=12 top, fifteen+three Visions=18 middle, remaining denizens bottom. Chronicle aid 12 denizens+2 is erroneous.
questions.observed_answer: Chronicle: Vision-only win chooses matching Oath; otherwise including multiple methods choose any except current. Exile winner flips all Citizen boards to Exile and may offer free Citizenship to other Exiles except just-flipped, not self; acceptor replaces each ruled-site garrison with exactly one winner-color warband. Rebuild top 10 denizens+2 Visions=12; middle 15+3=18; not 14.

fact_checks.expected_fact: Vision-only winner chooses matching Oath; other/multiple-method victory chooses a different Oath.
fact_checks.reason: The cited same-entry passage states the required rule, including its applicable conditions.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Vow an Oath:** won by Vision alone → next Oath matches that Vision. Any other way or multiple victory methods → choose any Oath **except current one**. Save goal in World Box.
2. **Free Chronicle Citizenship (ignore normal offers):** no Reliquary relic, resource payment or Scepter permission is required. If winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must do both: **flip their board to Citizen** and **replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site**, regardless of the old garrison size. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.
3. **Map and edifices:** Imperial winner may build **or** repair **one** edifice. At ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace denizen with matching intact Archive edifice, returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return relics to relic deck and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner does not rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside **all sites with ruins**, with attached ruins, remaining denizens and relics, in map order top Cradle to bottom Hinterland. Remove pawns/favor/secrets/warbands from map.
4. **Repack map slots:** excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland in top-down order. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots **bottom-up** with set-aside ruins **bottom-up**, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill any remaining slots with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top one up.
5. **Add 6 denizens:** winner's most common adviser suit determines 3 random Archive cards, next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise suit 1, to world deck. Choose among tied suits; no suited advisers → choose any. Suit cycle Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord. If Archive cannot supply the full allocation, do **not** add that allocation: heal Archive instead. Sort all Dispossessed by suit; take 6 random from largest Dispossessed suit stack into world deck; shuffle remaining Dispossessed into matching Archive suit stacks.
6. **Dispossess 6:** set aside all 5 Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles with **losers' advisers**, move 6 random cards unseen to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded from this pool.
7. **Relics:** save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to printed number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.
8. **Save world:** stack each site's attached cards on it, stack sites so top Cradle on top and bottom Hinterland at bottom, put in World Box. Save player boards on current Exile/Citizen sides. Next game may have different people: after seats are assigned, non-Chancellors choose among these boards on their saved sides in turn order, rather than automatically inheriting a particular person’s former board.
9. **Rebuild world deck:** shuffle all denizens remaining in play (not those retained at sites/Archive/Dispossessed). Top stack **10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12**; middle **15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18**; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. Chronicle aid's printed “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; do not make a 14-card top stack.

Rebuild top 10 denizens+2 Visions=12; middle 15+3=18; not 14.

Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots **bottom-up** with set-aside ruins **bottom-up**, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill any remaining slots with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top one up.
5. **Add 6 denizens:** winner's most common adviser suit determines 3 random Archive cards, next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise suit 1, to world deck. Choose among tied suits; no suited advisers → choose any. Suit cycle Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord. If Archive cannot supply the full allocation, do **not** add that allocation: heal Archive instead. Sort all Dispossessed by suit; take 6 random from largest Dispossessed suit stack into world deck; shuffle remaining Dispossessed into matching Archive suit stacks.
6. **Dispossess 6:** set aside all 5 Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles with **losers' advisers**, move 6 random cards unseen to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded from this pool.
7. **Relics:** save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to printed number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.
8. **Save world:** stack each site's attached cards on it, stack sites so top Cradle on top and bottom Hinterland at bottom, put in World Box. Save player boards on current Exile/Citizen sides. Next game may have different people: after seats are assigned, non-Chancellors choose among these boards on their saved sides in turn order, rather than automatically inheriting a particular person’s former board.
9. **Rebuild world deck:** shuffle all denizens remaining in play (not those retained at sites/Archive/Dispossessed). Top stack **10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12**; middle **15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18**; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. Chronicle aid's printed “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; do not make a 14-card top stack.

Chronicle: Vision-only win chooses matching Oath; otherwise including multiple methods choose any except current. Exile winner flips all Citizen boards to Exile and may offer free Citizenship to other Exiles except just-flipped, not self; acceptor replaces each ruled-site garrison with exactly one winner-color warband. Rebuild top 10 denizens+2 Visions=12; middle 15+3=18; not 14.

questions.question: Can you act at a remote ruled site to Muster/Trade, use a normal Action power there, or use a battle plan at your pawn site that you do not rule? How do persistent powers differ?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Muster/Trade only pawn site. Normal card power accessible by ruling card or pawn at its site, so remote ruled Action accessible. Battle plan requires rule, pawn alone insufficient. Persistent black-thick-braid power affects specified players ignoring ordinary access.
questions.observed_answer: Muster/Trade require eligible card at pawn site. Ordinary site Action power follows printed access (rule or pawn); persistent powers affect named players regardless access. Battle plan at site requires rule, not pawn presence.

fact_checks.expected_fact: Only at pawn site, so remote rule is insufficient.

evidence.excerpt: Place 1 favor on an **empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site** (no favor or secrets already). Gain 2 warbands from personal bank onto board; Citizens gain purple. Relics/ruins are ineligible. Rule is not required, and ruling a remote site does not allow remote Muster.

Muster/Trade require eligible card at pawn site. Ordinary site Action power follows printed access (rule or pawn); persistent powers affect named players regardless access. Battle plan at site requires rule, not pawn presence.

fact_checks.reason: The cited same-entry passage states the required rule, including its applicable conditions.

evidence.excerpt: Access a card's power if you rule it or your pawn is at its site; relic holders use held relics. evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

evidence.excerpt:
1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.
8. **Finish battle-plan effects for either winner:** defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally, discard any plans from either side that say “At end, discard.” A victorious defender gains no declared targets merely by defending. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

Incumbent keeps title on tie. If later behind and multiple leaders tie, outgoing holder chooses. Supremacy Chancellor holds for collective Empire. Transfer occurs at Campaign end, not temporary site-rule change.

If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.

Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.

May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.

Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.

If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Banishment itself supplies the no-Supply permission, including when a site normally sets a fixed Travel cost. Destination and non-Supply entry restrictions still apply unless a power ignores them. **Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice** if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go; that changes the destination decision, not the no-Supply payment.

If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects. If defender won, skip attacker’s targets but still resolve defender’s victorious effects. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.

questions.question: Which winner can build or repair an edifice in Chronicle, how many, where, and may a new edifice replace a denizen at a site already holding a ruin?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Only Chancellor/Citizen winner,one build or repair. Build at ruled site with no edifice intact or ruined,replace matching denizen by intact Archive edifice,denizen to world deck. Or repair ruled ruin by flipping intact. No building over an existing ruin.
